registration.name: 5G UE Registration
registration.intro: UE registers on the 5G network — SUCI identity concealment — 5G-AKA mutual authentication — NAS security activation

steps.title: Registration Request
steps.desc: UE encrypts its SUPI (permanent identity) using the Home Network Public Key (ECIES) to form SUCI — concealing its real identity over the air. A NAS Registration Request (type: Initial Registration) is sent to gNB over the 5G-NR Uu interface.

steps.title: NGAP: Initial UE Message
steps.desc: gNB selects an AMF from a configured list and wraps the NAS PDU in an NGAP Initial UE Message, forwarding it over the N2 interface (SCTP/IP). The message also carries gNB location and UE capabilities.

steps.title: Authentication Initiation
steps.desc: AMF discovers the correct AUSF via NRF, and sends Nausf_UEAuthentication_Authenticate Request. AMF provides the SUCI received from the UE. AUSF determines whether to use 5G-AKA or EAP-AKA' based on UDM policy.

steps.title: Auth Vector Request to UDM
steps.desc: AUSF calls Nudm_UEAuthentication_Get Request to UDM. UDM retrieves the UE's long-term key K from UDR, and generates a 5G Home Environment Authentication Vector: RAND, AUTN, HXRES* and KAUSF.

steps.title: Auth Vectors Returned
steps.desc: UDM returns the 5G HE AV to AUSF. AUSF stores HXRES* (to verify the UE's response later), derives KAUSF, and computes KAMF from it. RAND and AUTN are passed to AMF to be sent to the UE for mutual authentication.

steps.title: Auth Result Forwarded to AMF
steps.desc: AUSF returns the authentication result and KAMF to AMF. AMF will use KAMF to derive NAS security keys. AMF sends an Authentication Request down to the UE containing RAND and AUTN — UE verifies AUTN to authenticate the network.

steps.title: NAS Security Mode Command
steps.desc: AMF derives NAS keys: KNASenc (confidentiality) and KNASint (integrity) from KAMF. It sends a NAS Security Mode Command to the UE via gNB, selecting the ciphering and integrity algorithms. The UE verifies MAC and activates NAS security.

steps.title: Registration Complete
steps.desc: UE confirms with Security Mode Complete. AMF registers the UE, assigns a 5G-GUTI (Globally Unique Temporary Identifier), and sends a Registration Accept. The UE is now fully registered on the 5G network with an active security context.

pdu.name: PDU Session Establishment
pdu.intro: UE requests a PDU session to the internet — SMF selects UPF — PFCP rules programmed — N3 tunnel established — data flows

steps.title: PDU Session Establishment Request
steps.desc: UE sends a NAS PDU Session Establishment Request to gNB, specifying the target DNN (Data Network Name, e.g. internet), PDU session type (IPv4/IPv6/Ethernet), and the S-NSSAI for slice selection.

steps.title: AMF Receives Request
steps.desc: gNB forwards the NAS message to AMF over N2. AMF authorises the request against the UE's subscription (via UDM) and uses NRF service discovery to select the correct SMF for the requested DNN and slice.

steps.title: SMF: Session Context Creation
steps.desc: AMF sends Nsmf_PDUSession_CreateSMContext to SMF. SMF allocates a PDU Session ID, assigns a UE IP address from the UPF pool, selects a UPF using ULCL/branching rules, and contacts PCF for QoS policy (N7).

steps.title: UPF Programmed via PFCP
steps.desc: SMF sends a PFCP Session Establishment Request to UPF over N4. This programs UPF with Packet Detection Rules (PDRs) identifying traffic flows, Forwarding Action Rules (FARs), and QoS Enforcement Rules (QERs) for this session.

steps.title: UPF Confirms Rules Installed
steps.desc: UPF replies with PFCP Session Establishment Response, including the allocated F-TEID (Fully Qualified Tunnel Endpoint Identifier) for the N3 uplink tunnel — gNB will use this TEID to send user-plane data to UPF.

steps.title: SMF Returns Session Info to AMF
steps.desc: SMF sends the Create SM Context Response to AMF, including the UPF N3 TEID, QoS profiles (5QIs), and the UE's allocated IP address. AMF uses this to build the N2 resource setup for the gNB.

steps.title: gNB Configures Radio Resources
steps.desc: AMF sends N2 PDU Session Resource Setup Request to gNB with QoS profiles and the UPF N3 TEID. gNB allocates radio resources and configures Data Radio Bearers (DRBs), mapping QoS flows to bearers via SDAP.

steps.title: Session Accepted at UE
steps.desc: gNB sends RRC Reconfiguration + NAS PDU Session Establishment Accept to the UE, containing the assigned IP address, QoS rules, and DRB configuration. The PDU session is now established.

steps.title: Data Flowing — UE → gNB
steps.desc: UE sends IP packets uplink. The SDAP layer maps the QoS flow (QFI) to the correct DRB. PDCP/RLC/MAC/PHY layers encode and transmit over the NR air interface to gNB.

steps.title: Data Flowing — gNB → UPF via N3
steps.desc: gNB encapsulates the IP packet in GTP-U using the UPF's TEID and sends directly to UPF over N3. Important: AMF and SMF are control-plane only — user-plane data bypasses them entirely, flowing straight gNB → UPF.

steps.title: Data Flowing — UPF → Internet
steps.desc: UPF strips the GTP-U header, applies QoS enforcement (policing and shaping per QER), and routes the plain IP packet to the Data Network via N6. Full end-to-end 5G internet connectivity is now live.

vonr.name: VoNR Call Setup
vonr.intro: SIP INVITE flows through IMS — GBR QoS flow (5QI=1) established — RTP media streams active

steps.title: SIP INVITE — UE-A initiates call
steps.desc: UE-A sends a SIP INVITE to its IMS P-CSCF. The INVITE travels over the established IMS signalling PDU session (5QI=5, non-GBR). SDP offer includes UE-A's RTP port and supported voice codecs (AMR-WB, AMR-NB).

steps.title: INVITE via gNB-A → UPF
steps.desc: gNB-A encapsulates the SIP message in GTP-U and forwards to UPF over the N3 interface. UPF decapsulates and routes the SIP packet toward the IMS core P-CSCF over N6.

steps.title: P-CSCF Receives INVITE
steps.desc: P-CSCF receives the SIP INVITE. It signals PCF via the Rx interface to authorise and pre-reserve a GBR bearer for the upcoming voice media. S-CSCF performs routing lookup via I-CSCF and forwards the INVITE toward the called party.

steps.title: IMS Routes INVITE to Called Party
steps.desc: S-CSCF routes the SIP INVITE toward UE-B's P-CSCF. PCF is simultaneously triggered (via Rx) to establish the GBR QoS flow (5QI=1) for the voice bearer. The network pre-reserves resources before UE-B even answers.

steps.title: INVITE Delivered to UE-B
steps.desc: UE-B receives the SIP INVITE and the device rings. Simultaneously, SMF (triggered by PCF/Rx) establishes a GBR QoS flow at both UEs: PFCP session modification programs UPF with guaranteed 12.65 kbps for AMR-WB voice.

steps.title: 180 Ringing — UE-B is ringing
steps.desc: UE-B sends SIP 180 Ringing. The dedicated GBR DRB (5QI=1) has now been configured on gNB-B's air interface. The voice bearer is ready and waiting for the call to be answered.

steps.title: 180 Ringing Through IMS Core
steps.desc: IMS S-CSCF relays 180 Ringing toward UE-A. The GBR QoS flows are now active at both ends, providing guaranteed bandwidth even before the call is answered — this is a key feature of VoNR architecture.

steps.title: Ringing Reaches UE-A Side
steps.desc: UPF forwards the SIP 180 via N3 back to gNB-A. The GBR DRB for voice is now configured on gNB-A's air interface too. UE-A will hear the ringback tone momentarily.

steps.title: UE-A Hears Ringback
steps.desc: UE-A receives SIP 180 Ringing and plays the ringback tone locally. Both GBR voice bearers are fully established. The network is waiting for UE-B to answer...

steps.title: UE-B Answers — SIP 200 OK
steps.desc: UE-B user answers the call. SIP 200 OK is sent with SDP answer: selected codec AMR-WB (12.65 kbps), UE-B's RTP port for media. The 3-way SIP handshake is almost complete.

steps.title: 200 OK Routed Through IMS
steps.desc: IMS routes the 200 OK back to UE-A through the same SIP path. The GBR QoS flow (5QI=1) is fully confirmed active at both ends with guaranteed 12.65 kbps bandwidth and <100 ms packet delay budget.

steps.title: Call Active — RTP Media Flowing
steps.desc: UE-A sends SIP ACK completing the SIP 3-way handshake. RTP voice packets now flow bidirectionally peer-to-peer through the GBR QoS flows: UE-A ↔ gNB-A ↔ UPF ↔ gNB-B ↔ UE-B. HD VoNR call is live.

handover.name: Xn Handover
handover.intro: UE moves between gNBs — Source triggers direct Xn HO — AMF switches DL path via UPF — zero packet loss

steps.title: RRC Measurement Report
steps.desc: UE measures reference signals from neighbour cells. The A3 event triggers when Target gNB's RSRP exceeds Source gNB's RSRP by the configured offset (e.g. 3 dB) for the time-to-trigger duration. UE sends Measurement Report to Source gNB.

steps.title: Handover Request via Xn
steps.desc: Source gNB decides to hand over and sends XnAP Handover Request directly to Target gNB over Xn — no AMF involvement at this stage. The message carries the full UE context: security keys, QoS profiles, bearer config, and AS security context.

steps.title: Target gNB Accepts
steps.desc: Target gNB admits the UE, allocates radio resources (PRBs, DRBs), and configures PDCP/RLC entities. It replies with XnAP Handover Request Acknowledge containing a transparent RRC Reconfiguration container for Source gNB to forward to the UE.

steps.title: Handover Command to UE
steps.desc: Source gNB extracts the RRC container and sends RRC Reconfiguration (Handover Command) to the UE. The message contains: Target cell ID, dedicated RACH preamble, timing configuration, and DRB configurations for the new cell.

steps.title: UE Accesses Target gNB
steps.desc: UE performs contention-free RACH on Target gNB using the dedicated preamble (no collision risk). Target gNB responds with Timing Advance. UE sends RRC Reconfiguration Complete. The radio link is now established with Target gNB.

steps.title: Path Switch to AMF
steps.desc: Target gNB notifies AMF of the UE's arrival via N2 Path Switch Request, providing the new AN Tunnel Info (Target gNB N3 TEID). AMF contacts SMF over N11 to update the downlink user-plane path through UPF.

steps.title: UPF Path Redirected
steps.desc: SMF sends PFCP Session Modification Request to UPF: update the Forwarding Action Rule (FAR) to redirect downlink data from Source gNB's N3 TEID to Target gNB's new N3 TEID. UPF also sends GTP-U End Markers to Source gNB to flush its buffer.

steps.title: UPF Path Switch Confirmed
steps.desc: UPF confirms the path modification. Downlink data now flows to Target gNB via the new N3 tunnel. Any buffered data from Source gNB is forwarded to Target gNB via the pre-established data forwarding tunnel (part of Xn HO preparation).

steps.title: Handover Complete
steps.desc: AMF sends Path Switch Request Acknowledge to Target gNB. Source gNB resources are released via XnAP UE Context Release. The Xn Handover is complete — the entire procedure typically takes < 20 ms with zero user-plane packet loss.

deregistration.name: UE Deregistration
deregistration.intro: UE gracefully detaches from the 5G network — NAS context cleared — PDU sessions released — AMF notifies SMF/UDM

steps.title: UE Initiates Deregistration
steps.desc: UE sends a NAS Deregistration Request to gNB (type: Normal, Switch-Off, or USIM Removal). The request includes the 5G-GUTI so AMF can identify the UE context. Security headers protect the NAS message using the active NAS security context.

steps.title: gNB Forwards to AMF
steps.desc: gNB wraps the NAS PDU in an NGAP UL NAS Transport message and forwards it to the serving AMF over N2 (SCTP). AMF looks up the UE context using the 5G-GUTI and begins the deregistration procedure.

steps.title: AMF Releases PDU Sessions via SMF
steps.desc: AMF sends Nsmf_PDUSession_ReleaseSMContext to SMF for each active PDU session. SMF triggers UPF via PFCP Session Deletion to remove all PDRs, FARs, and QERs associated with this UE. The N3 GTP-U tunnel is torn down.

steps.title: UDM Notified of Deregistration
steps.desc: AMF calls Nudm_UECM_Deregistration to UDM, indicating the UE has deregistered. UDM clears the serving AMF registration for this SUPI. If the UE has a valid 5G-GUTI, UDM marks the identity as available for reassignment.

steps.title: UDM Confirms
steps.desc: UDM acknowledges the deregistration. The subscription data cached in AMF for this UE is now invalid. AMF will delete the UE context, including the 5G-GUTI, security contexts, and all bearer state, once the procedure completes.

steps.title: SMF Confirms Session Teardown
steps.desc: SMF confirms all PDU sessions are released. UPF has deleted all forwarding rules and the N6 interface connections are closed. Any allocated UE IP addresses are returned to the pool and are available for new sessions.

steps.title: AMF Sends Deregistration Accept
steps.desc: AMF sends a NAS Deregistration Accept to the UE via gNB. AMF then instructs gNB to release the RRC connection via NGAP UE Context Release Command. The N2 interface association for this UE is removed from gNB.

steps.title: RRC Connection Released
steps.desc: gNB sends RRC Release to the UE. The UE transitions to RRC_IDLE and clears its AS security context, radio bearer configuration, and stored 5G-GUTI. The UE is now fully detached. For switch-off type, no Deregistration Accept is sent — the UE powers off.

servicerequest.name: Service Request (Idle → Connected)
servicerequest.intro: UE in CM-IDLE resumes connectivity — RRC connection re-established — N2 context restored — user-plane path re-activated

steps.title: UE Initiates RRC Connection
steps.desc: UE in CM-IDLE/RRC_IDLE needs to send data or respond to paging. It initiates Random Access on the serving cell. After RA success, gNB sends RRC Setup. UE responds with RRC Setup Complete containing the NAS Service Request message.

steps.title: gNB Sends Initial UE Message to AMF
steps.desc: gNB forwards the NAS Service Request to AMF via NGAP Initial UE Message. The message includes the UE's 5G-GUTI for AMF context lookup. gNB has no existing N2 UE context yet — this is treated as an initial message even for returning UEs.

steps.title: AMF Requests User-Plane Activation
steps.desc: AMF authenticates the Service Request, verifies integrity protection, and sends Nsmf_PDUSession_UpdateSMContext to SMF for each PDU session to be re-activated. SMF needs to re-establish the N3 user-plane tunnel via UPF.

steps.title: UPF N3 Tunnel Re-activated
steps.desc: SMF sends a PFCP Session Modification Request to UPF to activate the uplink FAR (previously set to DROP in idle). UPF is updated with the new gNB N3 TEID so downlink traffic can be forwarded. The DL buffered packets will be released.

steps.title: UPF Ready
steps.desc: UPF confirms the session modification. The N3 GTP-U tunnel is now active. Any packets that were buffered in UPF during the idle period (triggered by a downlink data notification) are now queued for delivery to gNB.

steps.title: SMF Returns N2 Info to AMF
steps.desc: SMF returns the updated SM Context Response to AMF including the UPF N3 TEID and QoS profiles. AMF constructs the N2 PDU Session Resource Setup Request to send to gNB to re-establish the data radio bearers.

steps.title: gNB Configures DRBs
steps.desc: AMF sends N2 PDU Session Resource Setup to gNB. gNB sends RRC Reconfiguration to the UE to re-establish all Data Radio Bearers (DRBs) with PDCP/SDAP configuration. The UE responds with RRC Reconfiguration Complete.

steps.title: CM-CONNECTED — Data Flowing
steps.desc: UE is now CM-CONNECTED. All PDU sessions are active with full user-plane paths: UE ↔ gNB ↔ UPF ↔ DN. Buffered downlink data is flushed from UPF to gNB and delivered to the UE. The service request procedure is complete.

sliceselection.name: Network Slice Selection (NSSF)
sliceselection.intro: AMF queries NSSF to select the correct network slice — PCF authorises S-NSSAI — SMF assigned per slice

steps.title: UE Requests Slice in Registration
steps.desc: UE includes its Requested NSSAI in the NAS Registration Request. The NSSAI contains one or more S-NSSAIs (e.g. SST=1 eMBB, SST=2 URLLC). This tells the network which slices the UE wants to access in this registration area.

steps.title: AMF Queries NSSF for Slice
steps.desc: AMF calls Nnssf_NSSelection_Get to the NSSF, providing the UE's Requested NSSAI, Subscribed S-NSSAIs from UDM, the TAI (Tracking Area Identity), and any roaming info. NSSF determines the allowed slices and target AMF set.

steps.title: NSSF Queries NRF for NF Instances
steps.desc: NSSF calls Nnrf_NFDiscovery to find AMF instances (AMF Set) capable of serving the requested slices, and to discover SMF instances registered for each S-NSSAI/DNN combination. NRF maintains a live registry of all 5GC NF instances.

steps.title: NRF Returns NF Profiles
steps.desc: NRF returns a list of NF profiles matching the query — SMF instances registered for the S-NSSAI, their addresses, capacity, and supported DNNs. NSSF uses this to build the Allowed NSSAI and select the target AMF set for re-direction if needed.

steps.title: NSSF Returns Slice Decision to AMF
steps.desc: NSSF returns the Allowed NSSAI (the authorised subset of the requested slices), the Configured NSSAI for the serving PLMN, and optionally a target AMF set if the current AMF cannot serve the slice. AMF stores the Allowed NSSAI in the UE context.

steps.title: UE Requests PDU Session on Slice
steps.desc: When the UE later requests a PDU session, AMF uses the Allowed NSSAI to select the correct SMF for that S-NSSAI/DNN combination (discovered via NRF). AMF sends Nsmf_PDUSession_CreateSMContext to the slice-specific SMF instance.

steps.title: Slice-Specific Session Active
steps.desc: The slice-dedicated SMF establishes the PDU session with UPF and QoS policies appropriate for the slice (e.g. URLLC with ultra-low latency QER, or eMBB with high-bandwidth QoS). The UE's traffic is now isolated in its own network slice.

steps.title: Registration Accept Carries Slice Info
steps.desc: AMF sends NAS Registration Accept including the Allowed NSSAI so the UE knows which slices are active. The UE stores this for future PDU session requests. Slice isolation is now in effect — traffic for different S-NSSAIs flows through separate SMF/UPF chains.

sessionrelease.name: PDU Session Release
sessionrelease.intro: UE or network releases a PDU session — SMF tears down PFCP rules — UPF tunnel removed — IP address released

steps.title: UE Requests PDU Session Release
steps.iface: Uu — NAS PDU Session Release Request
steps.desc: UE sends a NAS PDU Session Release Request to gNB including the PDU Session ID to release. This can be UE-initiated (app closes, user disconnects) or network-initiated (network sends PDU Session Release Command first).

steps.title: gNB Forwards Release to AMF
steps.desc: gNB forwards the NAS Release Request to AMF over N2. AMF identifies the PDU session from the Session ID and selects the managing SMF. AMF then invokes the SMF to begin session teardown via the N11 interface.

steps.title: AMF Instructs SMF to Release Session
steps.desc: AMF sends Nsmf_PDUSession_ReleaseSMContext Request to SMF. SMF begins teardown: it notifies PCF via N7 to remove the policy session, then proceeds to delete the PFCP session at UPF, and releases the UE's IP address back to the pool.

steps.title: UPF Forwarding Rules Deleted
steps.desc: SMF sends PFCP Session Deletion Request to UPF. UPF removes all PDRs (Packet Detection Rules), FARs (Forwarding Action Rules), and QERs (QoS Enforcement Rules) for this session. The N3 GTP-U tunnel TEID is freed. The N6 path is closed.

steps.title: UPF Confirms Teardown
steps.desc: UPF returns PFCP Session Deletion Response with usage reports (bytes/packets sent/received) for billing/charging records. SMF passes CDR (Charging Data Record) information to the CHF (Charging Function) before completing the release.

steps.title: SMF Confirms to AMF
steps.desc: SMF sends Nsmf_PDUSession_ReleaseSMContext Response to AMF confirming the session is torn down. The SMF context for this PDU Session ID is deleted. AMF now instructs gNB to release the N2 resources and radio bearers.

steps.title: gNB Releases Radio Resources
steps.desc: AMF sends N2 PDU Session Resource Release Command to gNB. gNB sends RRC Reconfiguration to the UE to remove the DRB (Data Radio Bearer) and SDAP/PDCP configuration for this session. The radio resources are freed for other UEs.

steps.title: UE Confirms Release
steps.iface: Uu — NAS PDU Session Release Command
steps.desc: AMF sends NAS PDU Session Release Command to the UE (conveyed via gNB N2). UE responds with PDU Session Release Complete. The PDU session is now fully released — the UE's IP address is returned and no further data can flow on this session.

epsfallback.name: EPS Fallback (VoNR → VoLTE)
epsfallback.intro: VoNR call cannot be maintained on NR — network falls back to LTE/EPC — call continues on VoLTE

steps.title: VoNR Call Initiated on NR
steps.desc: UE initiates a VoNR call on the NR cell. gNB attempts to establish the GBR QoS flow (5QI=1) for voice. However, gNB determines NR coverage is insufficient (low SINR, no suitable NR cell for voice) and decides EPS Fallback is required.

steps.title: gNB Triggers EPS Fallback
steps.desc: gNB sends an NGAP message to AMF with an EPS Fallback Indicator, rejecting the QoS flow establishment and requesting a handover to LTE. AMF must now coordinate the inter-system handover from 5GC/NG-RAN to EPC/E-UTRAN via the N26 interface.

steps.title: AMF Contacts MME via N26
steps.desc: AMF sends a Forward Relocation Request to the target MME over N26. This is the 5GC↔EPC interworking interface. The message carries the UE's MM context, EPS bearer context mapped from 5G QoS flows, and the target LTE cell information.

steps.title: MME Prepares Target eNB
steps.desc: MME sends an S1AP Handover Request to the target eNB. The message contains the UE's AS security context (mapped keys from 5G KgNB to KeNB using the NH/NCC chaining), EPS bearer setup list, and the RRC Handover Command container.

steps.title: eNB Ready for UE
steps.desc: eNB allocates LTE radio resources and configures EPS bearers including the default bearer and GBR bearer for voice (QCI=1). It returns S1AP Handover Request Acknowledge with a transparent RRC Reconfiguration container for the UE.

steps.title: MME Responds to AMF
steps.desc: MME returns Forward Relocation Response to AMF including the RRC container and the target eNB's S1-U TEID for the downlink user-plane tunnel. AMF forwards the handover command to gNB to pass to the UE.

steps.title: UE Commanded to Move to LTE
steps.desc: gNB sends RRC Reconfiguration (Handover Command) to the UE with the target eNB configuration. The UE detaches from NR and performs RACH on the target LTE cell. UE sends RRC Connection Reconfiguration Complete to eNB confirming successful HO.

steps.title: Call Continues on VoLTE
steps.desc: UE is now connected to eNB on LTE with an active QCI=1 GBR bearer for voice. The IMS call continues seamlessly as VoLTE. The S-GW/P-GW user-plane path in EPC is active. The fallback is transparent to the end user — call audio is uninterrupted.

mtpaging.name: MT Paging (Mobile Terminated Call)
mtpaging.intro: Incoming call or data arrives for an idle UE — AMF pages across all cells in the tracking area — UE responds

steps.title: Downlink Data Arrives at UPF
steps.desc: A packet arrives from the internet destined for the UE's IP address. The UE is in CM-IDLE — its N3 GTP-U tunnel to gNB is suspended. UPF checks the FAR for this session and finds the action is BUFFER (set when the UE went idle). UPF buffers the packet.

steps.title: UPF Notifies SMF of Buffered Data
steps.desc: UPF sends a PFCP Session Report Request (Downlink Data Report) to SMF, indicating buffered downlink data is waiting for the UE. This is the trigger that starts the paging procedure to wake the UE from idle.

steps.title: SMF Requests AMF to Page UE
steps.desc: SMF calls Namf_Communication_N1N2MessageTransfer to AMF with a paging indication. The request includes the UE's SUPI, the PDU Session ID, and an N2 SM Information element so AMF knows which session triggered the page.

steps.title: AMF Pages All gNBs in Tracking Area
steps.desc: AMF sends NGAP Paging messages to all gNBs in the UE's last known Registration Area (RA). The paging message contains the 5G-S-TMSI (shortened GUTI) and a Paging DRX cycle. Each gNB broadcasts the page in the downlink over the PCCH logical channel.

steps.title: gNB Broadcasts Paging to UE
steps.desc: gNB schedules the Paging message in the Paging Occasion — a specific subframe determined by the UE's IMSI mod 1024 and the DRX cycle. UE wakes from DRX sleep to monitor PDCCH at its paging occasion and receives the Paging message with its 5G-S-TMSI.

steps.title: UE Responds with Service Request
steps.desc: UE recognises its own 5G-S-TMSI in the paging message and initiates RACH on the cell. After RA success, UE sends RRC Setup Complete containing a NAS Service Request. The UE is now transitioning from CM-IDLE to CM-CONNECTED.

steps.title: gNB Forwards Service Request to AMF
steps.desc: gNB sends NGAP Initial UE Message to AMF containing the NAS Service Request. AMF authenticates the request using the stored NAS security context (integrity check). AMF then triggers SMF to re-activate the user-plane path via PFCP session modification.

steps.title: User Plane Restored — Data Delivered
steps.desc: SMF sends PFCP Session Modification to UPF: change the FAR from BUFFER to FORWARD with the new gNB N3 TEID. UPF flushes the buffered downlink packets to gNB, which delivers them to the UE. The MT session is complete — the UE receives its data.
